headline: High: Firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling can leak or act on dbt-derived warehouse data, while shared file/MCP-style handoff creates prompt-injection and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core can expose model/output files and Firecrawl supports MCP-compatible client use plus interactive scraping APIs, so a shared handoff channel could let attacker-controlled content in Firecrawl influence dbt workflows. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, but the exact bridge is not directly evidenced, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are copied into Firecrawl prompts or MCP messages, injected instructions can propagate.
IF Firecrawl-scraped content is later parsed by dbt automation without provenance checks, prompt injection is plausible.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any Firecrawl output reaches dbt.
Prefix all imported content as untrusted in prompts and templates.
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in scraped text.
Use separate workspaces for dbt artifacts and Firecrawl outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and Firecrawl handles web content, screenshots, and API keys with broad egress. If warehouse outputs are exported into Firecrawl for scraping or debugging, sensitive data can leave the warehouse boundary through Firecrawl’s network path. The pairwise leak path is not directly documented, so uncertainty still warrants high due to Firecrawl’s broad egress.
conditions: IF warehouse-derived dbt artifacts are sent to Firecrawl APIs, sensitive data can be exfiltrated.
IF Firecrawl is given screenshots or API keys containing warehouse context, those secrets may be transmitted off-box.
mitigations: Keep dbt warehouse outputs out of Firecrawl inputs.
Rotate any API keys before using Firecrawl on sensitive environments.
Restrict Firecrawl to non-sensitive test data only.
Review outbound requests from Firecrawl for warehouse identifiers.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before any cross-agent transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core is not runnable here and only shows allowlisted egress to a data warehouse, while Firecrawl is runnable and supports multiple instances with broad API access. There is some overlap on mutable external resources, but no shared filesystem or direct write-to-same-dir capability is documented, so conflict risk is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable warehouse or API-backed dataset, concurrent updates may race.
IF an orchestrator shares a writable workspace between them, file-level conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate target resources to each agent.
Schedule dbt runs and Firecrawl runs sequentially.
Use read-only credentials for Firecrawl where possible.
Check for overlapping writes before each run.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can produce scraped content and structured data that dbt could ingest as upstream inputs, but dbt is not documented as critically validating those inputs. If Firecrawl returns malformed or misleading data, dbt transformations may propagate the error into downstream warehouse models. The interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is fed into dbt models without validation, bad scraped data can cascade downstream.
IF dbt jobs treat Firecrawl-derived tables as authoritative, incorrect facts may be published.
mitigations: Validate Firecrawl outputs before loading them into dbt.
Add schema checks on all scraped fields.
Quarantine new Firecrawl sources until reviewed.
Compare sampled records against source pages manually.
requires-engineering: add automated data-quality gates in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while Firecrawl handles web content, screenshots, and API keys and is documented with broad network egress. If regulated warehouse data is routed into Firecrawl, retention and residency obligations may diverge from the warehouse’s controls. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is exported into Firecrawl, retention and logging policies may diverge.
IF EU or PHI data is scraped or stored by Firecrawl, compliance review is required before use.
mitigations: Limit Firecrawl to non-regulated datasets.
Confirm retention settings before any export.
Document which data classes may cross into Firecrawl.
Review logs for sensitive identifiers after each run.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems.
